key_insight: FlowLet combines multi-scale wavelet decomposition with flow-matching generative modeling to efficiently synthesize high-quality, conditional 3D brain MRIs, enabling realistic age-conditional augmentation without heavy computational cost.
problem_solved: Addresses the scarcity and demographic imbalance of 3D brain MRI datasets that limit fair and generalizable Brain Age Prediction (BAP) models by providing a scalable, conditional synthetic-data generator.
method: Decompose 3D MRI volumes into multi-scale wavelet bands to reduce dimensionality and capture local/global structure.
Train a continuous-time flow-matching model in the wavelet domain to learn conditional velocity fields for synthesis (conditioning on age/metadata).

Reconstruct full-resolution 3D MRIs by inverting the wavelet transform after fast ODE-based sampling, yielding realistic, age-controllable volumes with lower memory and faster sampling than voxel-space models.
impact: Enables practical, privacy-preserving data augmentation for BAP and other neuroimaging tasks, improving dataset balance and downstream model fairness/generalization while reducing acquisition cost and compute.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: input MRI → wavelet decomposition → conditional flow-matching model → inverse wavelet → synthesized MRI
Before/after examples: side-by-side real vs. synthesized 3D slices or volume renderings across age groups

Icon set: 3D brain, wavelet/multi-scale symbol, fast-sampling stopwatch/GPU to convey efficiency
paper_title: FlowLet: Conditional 3D Brain MRI Synthesis using Wavelet Flow Matching
paper_authors: Danilo Danese, Angela Lombardi, Matteo Attimonelli, Giuseppe Fasano, Tommaso Di Noia
